title: Physics on arXiv — Friday, 16 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred, relevance-led selection rather than a popularity ranking; same-day citation evidence is limited.

sections.title: First Observation of the Radiative Decay D⁰ → γω
authors: BESIII Collaboration (M. Ablikim, M. N. Achasov, P. Adlarson, X. C. Ai, C. S. Akondi, et al.; 671 additional authors)
sections.abstract: The BESIII Collaboration reports a 6.0σ observation of D⁰ → γω, measuring its branching fraction as (2.12 ± 0.40(stat) ± 0.25(syst)) × 10⁻⁵.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete new decay observation with a reported 6.0σ significance and absolute branching fraction from 20.3 fb⁻¹ of BESIII data; ranked highly for the direct experimental result, not audience metrics.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say the branching fraction supports the dominance of long-distance hadronic dynamics in radiative charm decays and gives a benchmark for non-perturbative QCD calculations.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; 20.3 fb⁻¹ of e⁺e⁻ collisions at √s = 3.773 GeV recorded by BESIII, analyzed with a Particle Transformer-based strategy
sections.unique_caveat: The interpretation as a probe of long-distance dynamics is not itself a direct measurement of those dynamics; the branching fraction carries separate statistical and systematic uncertainties.

sections.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
sections.abstract: The authors use evaluator-guided evolutionary search, with LLM-proposed circuits, to reduce resource counts across quantum-computing tasks and find a new reversible architecture for modular inversion.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A cross-disciplinary method with reported improvements in seven of eight tasks and a new circuit architecture; ranked for breadth and testable resource claims, not measured readership.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report substantial reductions in Toffoli and qubit counts in seven tasks versus their state-of-the-art comparisons, plus a reversible divsteps-based modular-inversion architecture.
sections.evidence_type: computational; evaluator-scored circuit search across numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory
sections.unique_caveat: The claimed gains depend on the task set, evaluator, and comparison baselines; independent reproduction and hardware-level performance are not established by the abstract.

sections.title: Band-Resolved Superconducting Gaps via the Thermal Hall Effect in CeRu₂
sections.abstract: Thermal Hall transport, constrained by specific heat and normal-state magnetotransport, is used to assign the two reported superconducting gaps in CeRu₂ to different Fermi-surface sheets.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A specific experimental strategy addresses gap assignment in a multiband superconductor; the abstract reports numerical gap scales and a low-field sign reversal.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer Δe/kB ≈ 13 K on heavy Ce 4f electron sheets and Δh/kB ≈ 8 K on hole sheets from the thermal Hall response and supporting transport constraints.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; thermal Hall, specific-heat, and normal-state magnetotransport measurements
sections.unique_caveat: The assignment depends on the assumed two-band description and fitted gap/mobility parameters; the abstract does not report uncertainty ranges for the quoted gap values.

sections.title: LSST and Keck characterization of outer Main Belt comet P/2026 N2
sections.abstract: LSST and Keck observations find P/2026 N2 active across perihelion for 102 days, with imaging and dynamical modeling consistent with sustained or recurrent dust production.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Multiple observing epochs from LSST and Keck support a specific sustained-activity result, paired with archival-image and dynamical checks.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report active morphology over 102 days and similar corrected aperture brightness between July and October, supporting prolonged or recurrent dust production.
sections.evidence_type: observational; LSST June–July 2026, Keck/LRIS on 2026-10-07, archival DECam imaging, and a 5,000-particle dynamical integration
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed volatile sublimation, possibly water ice, is a hypothesis, not a confirmed mechanism; the comet's 2021 activity state is inconclusive.

sections.title: Operational Limits of Gravity-Mediated Entanglement
sections.abstract: A theoretical model studies how finite wave-packet width, dephasing, and residual electrostatic forces affect whether gravity-generated entanglement remains useful for operational tests.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Links quantum-information witnesses to practical gravitational-test imperfections and identifies concrete tolerance boundaries; placement reflects cross-field relevance and a clear experimental-design question.
sections.claimed_result: In a Gaussian-wave-packet, two-branch cat-state model, the authors find windows for Bell nonlocality and useful teleportation that shrink with broader packets or stronger dephasing; electrostatic phase can suppress the signal.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; Newtonian interaction averaged over finite-width packets with phenomenological correlated dephasing
sections.unique_caveat: Conclusions are model-dependent: the cat-state setup and phenomenological noise treatment do not establish that gravity-mediated entanglement has been observed.

sections.title: Numerical simulations of low-mass black hole-neutron star mergers with moderate eccentricities
sections.abstract: Numerical-relativity simulations test eccentric black-hole–neutron-star waveform models and examine how eccentricity and magnetic fields affect gravitational waves and merger remnants.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work compares waveform approximants against numerical-relativity simulations and quantifies impacts on tidal phase, disk mass, and disk oscillations, connecting modeling to gravitational-wave inference.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find reasonable agreement for SEOBNRv5EHM except when tidal effects matter, larger late-inspiral disagreement for tested post-Newtonian models, and efficient damping of trapped g-modes in strongly magnetized disks.
sections.evidence_type: computational; numerical-relativity merger simulations, including magnetized-matter cases
sections.unique_caveat: The study covers a subset of systems and a moderate-eccentricity range; waveform agreement is conditional, especially when tidal contributions become important.
